items.title: Prove or refute by execution that a hand-edited init-check.json passes the gate unchanged
items.context: Repro-first, and note the corrected premise: signInitCheck never takes agentResults as input, so the test is NOT the discarded draft's two-step 'tamper then re-sign' sequence. Test the one-step claim: in an isolated fixture (never a real story), edit agentResults directly, make NO init_check_set call, then check whether _hash still validates and whether the INIT->INIT_CHECK guard accepts it. Record the observed outcome even if it refutes the premise; a refutation re-scopes items 2-6 rather than being a failure. Probe the fallback-block-drop separately, checking it is lost after the FIRST ordinary call rather than when the attestationMode label flips.
items.userSees: node packages/main/tests/red/<artifact>.mjs prints one line per claim with RED/CONTROL-OK, ends with a RED count, and exits non-zero while the defect stands.

happy.desc: The artifact reproduces the PLAN probe: injected agentResults advances the gate with zero init_check_set calls

verification.selector: the gate ACCEPTS hand-injected reviewer coverage

edge.desc: The artifact also covers the issues field (erasing a recorded critical still advances), so a partial fix cannot turn it green

verification.selector: erasing a recorded blocking-severity issue leaves the file signature-VALID

adversarial.desc: It carries a SIGNATURE control (in-domain title edit must be rejected). If that control fails the run reports BROKEN and draws no conclusion, so a dead signature check cannot masquerade as this defect

verification.selector: SIGNATURE CONTROL: the gate REFUSES that in-domain edit as tampering

verificationEvidence.note: Runs the registered RED artifact through the product own validate runner (focused on the tag that selects it), so the row is produced by a real execution rather than asserted. The selector is the B3 claim marker, printed on every run regardless of verdict, so this evidence survives the CHK-002 fix instead of going stale the way a literal count would. On this tree that row reads RED: a hand-injected agentResults entry leaves the file signature-valid and the gate advances with zero init_check_set calls for it.

items.title: Bind agentResults and issues into the signature domain
items.context: signInitCheck at core/init-check-gate.ts:133-143 and recomputeInitCheckHash at :133-172. Both fields must be covered; fixing agentResults alone leaves an equivalent hole because the same edit can erase a recorded critical issue. Handle all six on-disk shapes (canonical pair, koala pair, two distinct @fallback pairs, three-entry historical-actor files, and files with no agentResults where initCheckAgentResults synthesizes from top-level fields). Decide explicitly what an absent field hashes to. CONDITIONAL ON CHK-001: if CHK-001's execution refutes the premise, re-scope this item before doing any of it rather than executing it as written.

items.title: Verify _hash before trusting previous.agentResults on read
items.context: store.readInitCheck (core/store.ts:566-572) is a bare readJson; the carry-forward at handlers/init-check.ts:138-142 trusts it. This does not cause the gate bypass but does admit data no caller wrote into a subsequently re-signed file. Decide what happens on mismatch: refusing to carry forward is not the same as refusing to read, and that difference decides whether the audit-only majority of the corpus becomes unreadable. CONDITIONAL ON CHK-001: if CHK-001's execution refutes the premise, re-scope this item before doing any of it rather than executing it as written.
items.userSees: A story whose init-check.json has a corrupted _hash reports the corruption by name rather than silently carrying the unverified records forward.

happy.desc: A _hash mismatch on read refuses to carry previous.agentResults forward

edge.desc: Reading a historical file with a legacy hash still RENDERS (story_get / audit paths work); refusing to trust is not refusing to read

adversarial.desc: A file whose _hash was recomputed by an attacker over tampered content is still refused, because the domain now covers the tampered fields

verificationEvidence.note: Row E3 of the registered RED artifact, run through the product own validate runner. The fixture hand-injects a reviewer record identified by a checkedAt marker no legal call can produce, then makes ONE ordinary init_check_set call by a DIFFERENT reviewer; the marker is absent from the newly signed record, so the unverifiable predecessor was refused rather than carried forward and re-signed. Selector is the marker name, not a count, so it stays re-earnable. Same run carries E0 (an UNTOUCHED predecessor is still carried forward verbatim and still advances) which rules out the degenerate fix of never carrying anything forward, and E2 (the written record is itself validly signed) which rules out the write simply breaking. Measured pre-fix on the same artifact: E3 RED.

items.context: handlers/init-check.ts:144-152 constructs the output without the fallback block written by init_check_repair (reason/actor/session/headHash). It is lost after the first ordinary call, before the initCheckAttestationMode label flips, so the durable evidence of a human attestation disappears earlier than the label advertising it. items.title: Choose and justify the migration position for the existing corpus
items.context: Re-derive the counts first; do not trust the background's figures. Structure of the argument: only files whose owning story is in INIT are operationally gated (canEnterInitCheckGuard early-returns otherwise, core/machine.ts:440) - at the measured commit that was 1 of 637 - so the real choice is one operational break versus roughly 636 audit-replay breaks. Critically, about 195 of 637 files carry a registry-invalid actor, overwhelmingly the pre-rename koala-review-story-init (zero occurrences in AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY), so re-signing the corpus by routing through the handler is not implementable and any design assuming it is must be rejected. CONDITIONAL ON CHK-001: if CHK-001's execution refutes the premise, re-scope this item before doing any of it rather than executing it as written.
